requirement.text:

source_documents.text:
I2



I2          Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
(August
(cont)
2006)       I2.1 General
(Rev.1
Jan 2007)   I2.1.1 Application*
(Corr.1
Oct 2007)   This UR applies to Polar Class ships according to UR I1.
(Rev.2
Nov 2010)   I2.1.2 Definitions
(Rev.3
Apr 2016)   I2.1.2.1 The length LUI is the distance, in m, measured horizontally from the fore side of the
(Rev.4      stem at the intersection with the upper ice waterline (UIWL) to the after side of the rudder
Dec 2019)   post, or the centre of the rudder stock if there is no rudder post. LUI is not to be less than
            96%, and need not be greater than 97%, of the extreme length of the upper ice waterline
            (UIWL) measured horizontally from the fore side of the stem. In ships with unusual stern and
            bow arrangement the length LUI will be specially considered.

            I2.1.2.2 The ship displacement DUI is the displacement, in kt, of the ship corresponding to the
            upper ice waterline (UIWL). Where multiple waterlines are used for determining the UIWL, the
            displacement is to be determined from the waterline corresponding to the greatest
            displacement.

source_documents.text:
I2.13.1 Application

         I2.13.1.1 A ramming impact on the bow is the design scenario for the evaluation of the
         longitudinal strength of the hull.




                                                       I2-17                       IACS Req. 2006/Rev.4 2019
                                                                                                             I2


         I2.13.1.2 Intentional ramming is not considered as a design scenario for ships which are
I2       designed with vertical or bulbous bows, see I1.1.6. Hence the longitudinal strength
(cont)   requirements given in I2.13 is not to be considered for ships with stem angle stem equal to or
         larger than 80 deg.

         I2.13.1.3 Ice loads are only to be combined with still water loads. The combined stresses
         are to be compared against permissible bending and shear stresses at different locations
         along the ship’s length. In addition, sufficient local buckling strength is also to be verified.

         I2.13.1.1 A ramming impact on the bow is the design scenario for the evaluation of the

                                                                                                             I2


         I2.13.1.2 Intentional ramming is not considered as a design scenario for ships which are
I2       designed with vertical or bulbous bows, see I1.1.6. Hence the longitudinal strength
(cont)   requirements given in I2.13 is not to be considered for ships with stem angle stem equal to or
